narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story of Israel in Egypt and the call of Moses.

the-lord.name: The Lord
the-lord.note: God speaking, from the burning bush and afterwards; majestic, patient, then stern.

moses.name: Moses
moses.note: Hebrew raised in Pharaoh's house, shepherd in Madian; hesitant and awed before God, pleading for his people.

jethro.name: Jethro (Raguel)
jethro.note: Priest of Madian, Moses' father in law; hospitable and kindly.

sephora.name: Sephora
sephora.note: Moses' wife, daughter of Jethro; urgent and distressed at the inn.

1.t: They will not believe me, nor hear my voice, but they will say: The Lord hath not appeared to thee.

2.t: What is that thou holdest in thy hand?

3.t: Cast it down upon the ground.
He cast it down, and it was turned into a serpent, so that Moses fled from it.

4.t: Put out thy hand, and take it by the tail.
He put forth his hand, and took hold of it, and it was turned into a rod.

5.t: that the Lord God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared to thee.

6.t: Put thy hand into thy bosom.
And when he had put it into his bosom, he brought it forth leprous as snow.

7.t: Put back thy hand into thy bosom.
He put it back, and brought it out again, and it was like the other flesh.

8.t: If they will not believe thee,
nor hear the voice of the former sign, they will believe the word of the latter sign.

9.t: But if they will not even believe these two signs, nor hear thy voice: take of the river water, and pour it out upon the dry land, and whatsoever thou drawest out of the river, shall be turned into blood.

10.t: I beseech thee, Lord, I am not eloquent from yesterday and the day before; and since thou hast spoken to thy servant, I have more impediment and slowness of tongue.

11.t: Who made man's mouth? or who made the dumb and the deaf, the seeing and the blind? did not I?

12.t: Go therefore, and I will be in thy mouth; and I will teach thee what thou shalt speak.

13.t: I beseech thee, Lord, send whom thou wilt send.

14.t: The Lord being angry at Moses, said:
Aaron the Levite is thy brother, I know that he is eloquent: behold he cometh forth to meet thee, and seeing thee, shall be glad at heart.

15.t: Speak to him, and put my words in his mouth: and I will be in thy mouth, and in his month, and will shew you what you must do.

16.t: He shall speak in thy stead to the people, and shall be thy mouth: but thou shalt be to him in those things that pertain to God.

17.t: And take this rod in thy hand. wherewith thou shalt do the signs.

18.t: Moses went his way, and returned to Jethro his father in law, and said to him;
I will go and return to my brethren into Egypt, that I may see if they be yet alive.

19.t: And the Lord said to Moses, in Madian:
Go, and return into Egypt; for they are all dead that sought thy life.

20.t: Moses therefore took his wife, and his sons, and set them upon an ass; and returned into Egypt, carrying the rod of God in his hand.

21.t: And the Lord said to him as he was returning into Egypt:
See that thou do all the wonders before Pharao, which I have put in thy hand: I shall harden his heart, and he will not let the people go.

22.t: And thou shalt say to him: Thus saith the Lord: Israel is my son, my firstborn.

23.t: I have said to thee: Let my son go, that he may serve me, and thou wouldst not let him go: behold I will kill thy son, thy firstborn.

24.t: And when he was in his journey, in the inn, the Lord met him, and would have killed him.

25.t: Immediately Sephora took a very sharp stone, and circumcised the foreskin of her son, and touched his feet, and said:
A bloody spouse art thou to me.

26.t: And he let him go after she had said:
A bloody spouse art thou to me, because of the circumcision.
26.q: "because of the circumcision" kept in her speech as the Douay punctuates it; it may be the narrator's explanation

27.t: And the Lord said to Aaron:
Go into the desert to meet Moses.
And he went forth to meet him in the mountain of God, and kissed him.

28.t: And Moses told Aaron all the words of the Lord, by which he had sent him, and the signs that he had commanded.

29.t: And they came together, and they assembled all the ancients of the children of Israel.

30.t: And Aaron spoke all the words which the Lord had said to Moses: and he wrought the signs before the people.

31.t: And the people believed. And they heard that the Lord had visited the children of Israel, and that he had looked upon their affliction: and falling down they adored.
